mission: Deliver the deployment story for the g10/g11 consent DB role separation: IaC secrets/ECS wiring in the in-repo Terraform, an operations runbook (role provisioning, credential rotation, migration procedure, residual risk), and an honest STATUS_BOARD f23 update — internal preparation complete, only production credential application external.
method: Terraform (infra/terraform): the data module now generates 4 per-role 32-char random passwords and 4 KMS-encrypted Secrets Manager secrets holding full connection URLs (<env>/db-url-app|worker|migrator|readonly), composed from the RDS endpoint; the compute module injects DATABASE_URL_APP into the api task and DATABASE_URL_WORKER into the media-worker task as ECS container secrets (matching the env vars services/api/src/config.ts and services/media-worker/src/main.ts already read from g10), and scopes the task-execution role to secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on exactly those two ARNs plus kms:Decrypt on the data key — the migrator and readonly secrets are not readable by service tasks. Migrations stay a deliberate operator step (never wired into task definitions). New docs/RUNBOOK_CONSENT_DB_ROLES.md covers the role model, IaC wiring, provisioning SQL for staging/production (mirroring init-roles.sql with Secrets Manager passwords), the g11-measured pgcrypto admin prerequisite, one-role-at-a-time rotation with terraform -replace + ALTER ROLE + forced ECS redeploy, the migrator-credential migration procedure, and an explicit residual-risk section. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and docs/STATUS_BOARD.md (f23 row + open-findings note) updated to match.
datasetScope: Not a dataset experiment: deployment/IaC/documentation workstream. No annotation data, no gold labels, no cascade metrics involved.
holdoutStatement: Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were not touched, read, listed, or referenced. This workstream involves no video/label data at all.

configuration.terraform: v1.9.8 (fmt + init -backend=false + validate on infra/terraform/envs/staging; no AWS credentials used or required)

terraform.validate: Success! The configuration is valid. (envs/staging, terraform 1.9.8, init -backend=false)
terraform.plan: NOT run — requires AWS credentials (external); validate is the strongest in-repo check

findings: The in-repo Terraform architecture permits real wiring, not just a plan: per-role connection-URL secrets in the data module, ECS container-secret injection in the compute module, and least-privilege execution-role scoping all validate with terraform validate — no placeholder IaC needed.

The AWS Terraform provider cannot create in-database Postgres roles; role provisioning is therefore a documented operator SQL step (runbook §3) using the Terraform-generated passwords, keeping Terraform state free of any in-database dependency.

Rotation never touches grants: privileges live on the NOLOGIN group roles, so ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD plus a forced ECS redeploy is the whole rotation; the runbook pins the ordering hazard (secret and database disagree between -replace and ALTER ROLE).
Migrations are deliberately excluded from ECS task wiring so a compromised runtime cannot replay DDL; the migrator secret is unreadable by the service execution role by construction.

Residual risk stated explicitly: the RDS master user (rds_superuser) and AWS account admins can bypass every in-database boundary; that cloud-superuser power cannot be removed from inside this repository — BLOCKED_EXTERNAL.
verdictRationale: Everything buildable in-repo is built and verified: Terraform wiring validates (terraform validate green), the runbook covers provisioning/rotation/migration/residual-risk end-to-end grounded in the g11 measured prerequisites, docs updated honestly, and all root + mobile gates pass on the branch. PROVISIONAL rather than GREEN because terraform plan/apply and the actual role provisioning require production/staging AWS credentials that do not exist in this repo — only that credential application is external, and the cloud-superuser bypass remains BLOCKED_EXTERNAL regardless.
